text:
anita: Heads-up — PR #4567 (api-reference) has a broken multipart example. The curl snippet sets a boundary of '----WebKitFormBoundaryXYZ' but the Ruby Faraday example uses a different boundary. That will confuse users trying file uploads.

rachel: ah thanks, spotted in review. I ran the curl example and the server rejects the payload.

kevin: can you paste the snippets? I can push a tiny patch.

anita: sure — from the PR: 
```
# curl from docs (broken)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/files \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundaryXYZ" \
  --data-binary $'------WebKitFormBoundaryABC\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="test.txt"\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\nhello\r\n------WebKitFormBoundaryABC--'
```

and the Ruby example in the same page: 
```ruby
# Ruby Faraday example (uses library boundary)
conn = Faraday.new(url: 'https://api.redwood.ai')
resp = conn.post('/v1/files') do |req|
  req.headers['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{ENV['TOKEN']}"
  req.body = { file: Faraday::FilePart.new('test.txt', 'text/plain') }
end
```

matt: yep the curl body uses ABC but header says XYZ — that's the mismatch. Also the curl is using --data-binary with a literal multipart payload which is fragile. We should either: 1) show curl using --form (-F) which lets curl set the boundary, or 2) make both examples show the same explicit boundary. Prefer #1.

rachel: agree. For docs consistency, switch curl to -F and add a short note: "Use -F so curl chooses the boundary; this avoids manual errors."

kevin: I'll open a tiny follow-up PR to replace the manual body with `-F "file=@test.txt"` and remove the explicit Content-Type header. Should I also update the Ruby snippet to show `multipart/form-data` explicit header?

anita: don't set Content-Type manually for curl. For Ruby, keep the Faraday example as-is (it sets boundary automatically). But add a comment in the Ruby block: `# Faraday sets the multipart boundary for you` so readers know why we don't show it.

docs-bot: PR suggestion: add a changelog entry to the patch noting "fix multipart examples (curl/Ruby) to avoid mismatched boundary". Also run docs tests (link-checker, markdown-lint) — I queued them. :robot_face:

matt: one extra ask — update the API note that accepts multipart: server will accept any boundary but examples should not show contradictory values. Tiny editorial touch: replace the manual multi-line payload with `-F` example and add expected 201 response snippet.

kevin: makes sense. I'll include the 201 response sample in the patch. Planning to push in ~10m.

rachel: awesome. @anita can you review the follow-up PR once it's up? Want to get this shipped before the docs deploy tomorrow.

anita: yep will review. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
